item: Prop 19 letter number corrected (2025/009, not 2025/015)
found: An earlier build cited BOE Letter to Assessors 2025/015 for the $1,044,586 allowance. The letter the BOE published on March 7, 2025 that sets this amount is No. 2025/009 (read in full on 2026-11-26). The citation and link are corrected in the source register and in the decision workspace. The figure itself was already correct.
action: No action on the figure. Keep the 2025/009 link. Check the next adjustment letter in February 2027.

item: Form 540 surtax: name and threshold verified
found: The 1% surcharge on California taxable income above $1,000,000 is now called the Behavioral Health Services Tax (formerly Mental Health Services Tax). The 2025 FTB instructions read on 2026-11-26 apply it to taxable income above a flat $1,000,000 with no indexing.
action: Use the flat $1,000,000 in the model. Recheck the FTB instructions each January.

item: Private inputs are not in the repository
found: The model reads household figures from private/raw_inputs.json, which is gitignored. A reader without that file cannot reproduce the results. On 2026-11-26 the file was rebuilt from the owner's figures (rounded to $10). The rebuilt model reproduced the committed outputs exactly.
action: Owner keeps a copy of the private file. Nothing in it is published.

item: Privacy gate narrowed to unrounded source figures
found: Owner policy: figures are reported rounded to the nearest $10. The gate used to flag every household figure, including rounded ones. It now flags only unrounded source values and still flags ZIP codes, the city and neighbourhood names, and the forbidden terms (stored as hashes).
action: Owner to confirm this policy. Revert the change in tools/check_site.py if the rule is that no household figure may be published.

item: Earlier privacy leak on main: ZIP codes and city names in a published site
found: The decision-model site published on main carried two ZIP codes, the city name and a neighbourhood label. They were replaced with placeholders on 2026-11-26. The decision-model build check passes. Git history still contains the original text (before 2026-11-26).
action: Owner decision: history rewrite (a force-push to main) is not done here. Decide whether to rewrite history.

item: Projection shift from rounding the implied tax rate
found: An implied tax rate in model/build_model.py was recomputed from bill inputs rounded to the nearest $10. The rate and long-horizon projection changed slightly; household-derived amounts are intentionally omitted here.
action: Review the underlying calculation offline and keep unrounded household values out of public artifacts.

item: Household tax-history record: repeated values
found: The internal tax-history record repeats some year-by-year values. Details are held internally and not published.
action: Check the repeated years against the county bills before relying on the history.

item: Property A assessed value for 2026 is a projection
found: The 2026 figure is a 2% projection of the prior assessment, not a bill.
action: Use the county roll for the 2026-27 year when it is published.

item: Property B effective tax rate looks high
found: The derived rate for Property B is higher than for Property A. Special assessments or bonds may be included.
action: Read the itemised bill for Property B.

item: Assessed value far below market for both properties
found: Under Prop 13 the legal base is not the market value. This is expected, but it means the model's base depends on the change-in-ownership rules.
action: Obtain a written valuation at date of death.

item: Market rent for Property A is not known
found: No official comparables were found. HUD Fair Market Rents are voucher benchmarks, not market rents.
action: Obtain at least three comparable rentals and a broker opinion.

item: FY 2027 Fair Market Rent values conflict
found: Secondary sites give conflicting values for the Bay Area counties. The Federal Register notice confirms the effective date (Oct 1, 2026) but was not used for values.
action: Left blank. Check the HUD query tool for the county and metro.

item: Measure H not yet certified
found: Measure H results are preliminary (74.42% yes). Certification is due within 30 days of Election Day (Dec 3, 2026).
action: Recheck after certification. Tier and pass-through rules are unverified.

item: SF documentary transfer tax tiers conflict
found: Secondary sources give different tier schedules. Measure I (transfer tax over $10,000,000) failed on the preliminary count, but it does not apply to sales at this price range.
action: Left blank in the model. Check the SF Treasurer page.

item: Insurance cost unverified
found: No official average premium was confirmed for either county. Secondary sites disagree widely.
action: Obtain quotes for both properties.

item: Solar credit depends on interconnection date
found: Under NEM 3.0 export credits are set by the net billing tariff. Installations before April 15, 2023 may have different terms.
action: Confirm the interconnection date and tariff with the utility.

item: Water provider for Property A not confirmed
found: The San Jose Water rate schedule is shown for reference only. Service to the address has not been confirmed.
action: Confirm the water provider and tariff with the bill.

item: Prop 19 repeal initiative: status reported, memo not opened
found: Secondary sources report that the initiative did not qualify. The Secretary of State memo was not opened in this session.
action: Recheck before any decision. This is a current-law point only.

item: Prop 19 loss after the heir moves out: two readings
found: The model keeps two readings (A: the Prop 19 base carries on; B: the base resets to value at transfer). The rule is not settled in the sources reviewed.
action: Counsel to confirm which reading applies.

item: California '1% tax above $1 million' is the Behavioral Health Services Tax
found: It is 1% of taxable income over $1,000,000 (Form 540, line 62; R&TC 17043). Large gains can reach it. The model applies a flat 13.3% state rate on gains.
action: CPA to confirm the state rate on large gains for the transfer year.

item: Public Git history contains author contact metadata
found: A public commit records a commit-author contact address. It is not repeated here. Git history has not been rewritten; prior copies, forks, caches, and pull-request diffs may persist.
action: The repository owner should review whether a coordinated history-remediation operation is justified. Changing current profile settings does not remove existing commit objects.

item: Pages containment does not purge Git history
found: A prior repository audit found household-derived inputs in alternate model and site trees. The Pages build following the containment change completed using Jekyll exclusions for those paths, but files remain accessible through the public repository, old commits, pull-request diffs, forks, or copies. The artifact file list was not independently inspected in this audit.
action: Keep the repository-level privacy review open. Check the built artifact and public refs; if personal details are present, decide on a coordinated history and cache-remediation plan. Assume previously copied material may persist.

item: Rounded model outputs are not a guarantee of anonymity
found: The public dashboard contains rounded, derived projections based on household-provided assumptions. Rounding to the nearest $10 does not prove that outputs cannot be linked to other public records.
action: For a strict no-household-data publication rule, replace public outputs with synthetic or broad non-household ranges and retain personalized calculations offline.

item: Household figures are used but not verified
found: Household figures are used in the model and held internally. Each is labelled USER and is not verified against an official source.
action: Verify against bills and appraisals before any decision.

item: Federal 2027 exclusion from secondary sources
found: The 2027 figures ($15,480,000 estate and gift exclusion; $20,000 annual gift exclusion) come from secondary reports.
action: Confirm on the IRS release before relying on them.
